result.title: Harnessing Language Models as Optimization Modeling Agents
result.summary: Large language models (LLMs) can translate natural-language optimization problems into solver programs, but reliably producing correct formulations and implementations remains challenging. Existing approaches improve optimization modeling through agentic workflows or task-specific post-training. This raises a practical question: can a lightweight harness using a single model role achieve competitive performance without additional training? We introduce OPTICYCLE and OPTISTATE, two lightweight inference harnesses for optimization modeling, and evaluate them on nine benchmarks comprising 2,634 problems using 11 Qwen variants spanning 0.6B-27B parameters. Our results show that execution-guided revision consistently improves macro accuracy over direct generation for all evaluated models, with gains of up to 49.46 percentage points. Despite their simplicity, both harnesses outperform six adapted agentic workflows in same-model comparisons and four evaluated post-trained optimization models at comparable model sizes, without additional training. Explicit formulation state provides further but model-dependent improvements, suggesting that additional structure is not universally beneficial.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 OPTICYCLE 与 OPTISTATE 两种轻量推理框架，在 9 个基准、2634 道题和 11 个 Qwen 模型（0.6B–27B）上检验免训练的单角色 harness 能否做好优化建模；结果显示执行引导的修订普遍优于直接生成，显式建模状态带来的额外收益则依赖模型。
AI.relevance_reason: 与视觉 latent 推理无直接关联，但其「执行反馈驱动修订」与显式中间状态的可供核查线索，可能对应 LVR 中状态更新、验证驱动的迭代精化与何时停止修订的决策问题。
